title: Ephemeral credential flow, rotation automation, and dev ergonomics for SDKs
creator: Alex Chen
description: Problem: Customers and internal SDKs currently rely on long-lived API keys stored in environment variables or vaults. This causes operational friction for enterprise SSO users, increases blast radius when keys leak, and makes local dev harder for contributors. Goal: Design and implement an SDK-level abstraction and migration plan that supports ephemeral API keys, automatic rotation, SSO token passthrough for enterprise customers, secure local-dev fallbacks, and clear guidance/examples in Python/TypeScript/Go. Deliverables include: (1) credential provider interface across SDKs, (2) built-in refresh middleware for streaming and non-streaming calls, (3) examples for ephemeral key issuance and silent refresh with SSO sessions, (4) migration guide and automation playbook for rotating existing keys, and (5) acceptance tests and a security review artifact.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a unified CredentialProvider abstraction with at least: StaticKey, EphemeralKey (with TTL), SSOAdapter (token exchange), and EnvFallback
HTTP/Streaming transports automatically perform transparent refresh with exponential backoff and jitter on 401/403 indicating expired credentials
Local dev flow works offline: CLI 'rw login-dev' issues a short-lived developer token and documents safe storage options (OS keychain, dev-only file with restricted perms)
Migration playbook and automation scripts rotate 80% of active keys for internal activity without customer impact using canary rollout
Security review completed and approval attached to this ticket

notes: Design rationale: Ephemeral tokens reduce blast radius and enable short TTLs for public workloads. For enterprise SSO, we avoid storing raw SAML/OIDC refresh tokens in SDKs — instead SDKs will accept a short-lived exchange token issued by the customer's SSO connector (brokered via the control plane) or use the browser-based OIDC flow provided by the Console.

Backoff policy: use decorrelated jitter (base=200ms, cap=5s, multiplier=2) for refresh attempts. If refresh fails repeatedly with non-recoverable error codes (401 with 'invalid_grant' or 403 'account_disabled'), surfacing a clear error to the integrator is required.

Streaming considerations: for streaming RPCs that carry an Authorization header, refresh should attempt a silent token refresh and if successful inject new token via re-auth handshake (we'll use standard 'reconnect-with-token' control frame for WS streams). For strictly non-reconnectable transports, the SDK should surface a termination with a specific error code and automatic retry behavior controlled by user option 'autoRetryOnAuthFailure'.

Local dev: no automatic sync of developer tokens to production stores. CLI warns when pushing tokens to remote registries or CI. The 'rw login-dev --export' option will print a one-time ephemeral token for CI use; recommended pattern is to configure CI to call token-service with ephemeral service accounts instead of exporting developer tokens.

Migration plan highlights: identify long-lived keys via usage dashboard over 30-day window, schedule rolling rotation in waves of 5% of keys every 12h with canary check on error rate and 5xx rate. Have automatic fallback to legacy key verification for 48h during rollout to avoid user-facing errors.

Testing: add integration tests that emulate token service downtime and verify SDK token refresh backoff and graceful degradation. Add chaos test where token-service returns 500 for a window and we assert SDK does not leak sensitive headers into logs.
implementation_notes: Python: provide CredentialProvider ABC with 'get_authorization_header() -> str' and 'close()' for cleanup. EphemeralKey caches token and refreshes proactively in background thread. Use threading.Event to wake on shutdown.

TypeScript: export credentialMiddleware(fetchOptions) which augments headers and subscribes to a TokenRefresher singleton with event emitter for token updates. For Node and Deno use native Keytar for keychain storage when available.

Go: provide interface type CredentialProvider { GetAuthHeader(ctx context.Context) (string, error) } and a Transport wrapper that injects header. Use context cancellation to abort refreshes on shutdown.
Telemetry: emit non-sensitive metrics: token_refresh_attempts, token_refresh_success, token_refresh_failure, token_expiry_proactive_refresh_count. Do not log token values or raw auth headers.
Error surfaced to integrator: SDK uses a structured error code 'REDWOOD_AUTH_EXPIRED' with helpful recovery suggestions (call rw login-dev or check SSO session)
